reason: The pancreatic cells are labelled to release insulin when blood glucose is higher, matching the first goal.
expectation: The higher-glucose blood should trigger insulin release.

effect: Higher glucose led to insulin entering the blood, so I can follow its route to muscle.
reaction: The picture makes the message's destination clear.
reason: The muscle fibres have receptors facing blood-carried insulin, and the goal is to store glucose in muscle.

choice.with: Muscle fibres beside a blood vessel

expectation: Insulin should help the muscle take in glucose and store some of it.

effect: Insulin helped muscle store glucose as linked chains while remaining outside the cells. The remaining goal is the liver's response to lower glucose.
reaction: It was useful to see that insulin is the message, not part of the store.
reason: The pancreatic cells are labelled to release their other hormone when blood glucose is lower.
expectation: The lower-glucose blood should trigger release of the liver's chemical message.

effect: Lower glucose triggered a blood-carried message to the liver, which can help break down its carbohydrate store.
reaction: The labelled route makes the next pairing clear.
reason: The hormone's label says it tells the liver to release glucose, and the liver store contains linked glucose units.
expectation: The message should help the liver break down its store and release glucose.

effect: The liver's store became smaller as glucose entered the blood, completing the between-meals route. The release signal also eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: Seeing the store shrink made the result easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Sending insulin to muscle was most worthwhile: it showed glucose becoming a store while insulin remained a message outside the cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two pancreatic-cell pairings felt somewhat repetitive, although they showed responses to different blood-glucose levels.

surprise.text: I was surprised that insulin stayed outside the muscle cells rather than becoming part of the stored material.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but the second hormone was only called the liver-release hormone; its specific name was not explained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: comparing the muscle and liver routes made the connections understandable, and I would be curious to see another body regulation example.
